title: 0/1 Knapsack
statement: You are given a list weights and a list values of equal length, where item i has weight weights[i] and value values[i], plus an integer capacity for a knapsack. Each item may be used at most once (0/1 knapsack). Return the maximum total value achievable without the total weight exceeding capacity. If there are no items or capacity is 0, the answer is 0.
hints: For each item you only have two choices — leave it out or take it — and taking it uses up part of the remaining capacity, so track best value as a function of both how many items you've considered and how much capacity remains.

Let dp[i][c] be the best value achievable using the first i items with capacity c. dp[i][c] = dp[i-1][c] (skip item i) or, if it fits, dp[i-1][c-weight[i]] + value[i] (take item i) — take the max of the two.

Build a table dp of size (n+1) x (capacity+1) initialized to 0; for each item i from 1 to n, for each capacity c from 0 to capacity, set dp[i][c] = dp[i-1][c], and if weights[i-1] <= c also compare against dp[i-1][c-weights[i-1]] + values[i-1]; return dp[n][capacity].
